claim: Xi Jinping made a state visit to Brasília on 20 Nov 2024 (after the G20 Rio summit), where he and Lula signed 37 agreements spanning trade, agriculture, industry, energy, science and health and linked China's Belt and Road with Brazil's PAC/Nova Indústria Brasil plans.

Lula made a state visit to Beijing on 10-13 May 2025 (his 4th official China trip); the two governments signed 20 agreements and ApexBrasil announced R$27bn of Chinese corporate investment pledges (incl. R$6bn from GWM).

Brazil–China trade hit a record US$171bn in 2025 (+8.2% y/y); Brazilian exports to China were ~US$100bn, 28.7% of Brazil's total exports, the second-highest on record after US$104bn in 2023; soybeans were over one-third of the value.

China imported zero US soybeans in September 2025, the first zero month since Nov 2018 (vs 1.7 Mt in Sep 2024), and as of mid-Sep 2025 had made no purchases of US new-crop soybeans; Jan–Sep 2025 imports from Brazil were 63.7 Mt.
China imported a record 111.8 Mt of soybeans in 2025 (+6.5%); Brazil supplied 82.3 Mt, a 73.6% share (vs 71% in 2024), per GACC data published 20 Jan 2026.

claim: The White House fact sheet on the Trump–Xi Busan deal (30 Oct 2025) states China will buy at least 12 Mt of US soybeans in the last two months of 2025 and at least 25 Mt in each of 2026, 2027 and 2028, and will 'effectively eliminate' its rare-earth export controls.
China reached the ~12 Mt US soybean purchase target only in early 2026 (deadline effectively extended to end-February), via state buyers Sinograin and COFCO, with cargoes shipping December–May.
Trump made a state visit to China on 13-15 May 2026 (not April); the White House said China would buy at least US$17bn/yr of US farm goods through 2028 on top of the Oct 2025 soybean commitments.

Xi made a state visit to Washington on 24-25 Sep 2026; the US–China Busan truce was extended to 10 Jan 2027, a '30 for 30' tariff-cut framework (~1,600 products, US$30bn) was identified that excludes soybeans, existing 10% tariffs stay, and two more Trump–Xi meetings are planned for Nov and Dec 2026.

As of late Sep 2026, USDA export-sales data show ~10.2 Mt of US soybeans committed to China for the 2026-27 marketing year against the 25 Mt annual pledge; the US$17bn non-soy farm commitments are described as behind schedule.

China took 69% of Brazil's soybean exports in H1 2026 vs 75% in H1 2025 (48.3 Mt shipped to China), while Brazil's total soybean exports grew >8% as cargoes were redirected to Europe, Middle East and SE Asia.
MOFCOM opened a global safeguard investigation into imported beef on 27 Dec 2024 (requested by China Animal Agriculture Association), extended twice (to 26 Nov 2025, then 26 Jan 2026).

On 31 Dec 2025 (MOFCOM Announcement No. 87) China imposed a 3-year beef safeguard from 1 Jan 2026: country quotas totalling ~2.7 Mt in 2026 with a 55% extra tariff above quota; Brazil's quota is 1.106 Mt (2026), 1.128 Mt (2027), 1.151 Mt (2028); Australia 205 kt, US 164 kt.

Brazil filled its 1.1 Mt Chinese beef quota by end-Sep 2026 and China began charging the extra 55% (67% total with the 12% MFN duty) on Brazilian beef from 1 Oct 2026; China rejected Brazil's lobbying (May 2026) to use other countries' unused quota (e.g. Uruguay's).

ABIEC: China bought 1.68 Mt of Brazilian beef in 2025 (48% of Brazil's beef exports), worth US$8.9bn of US$18.3bn total; the 2026 quota covers ~65% of 2025 volume and ABIEC expects total Brazilian beef exports to fall ~10% in 2026.
MOFCOM announced on 22 Jul 2026 that Brazilian beef had reached 80% of its 1.1 Mt safeguard quota, saying the measure aims to help domestic industry 'rather than restrict normal trade'.

2021 atypical BSE suspension (Bolsonaro govt): Brazil halted beef exports to China on 4 Sep 2021 under protocol after two atypical cases (MG, MT); China authorised resumption on 15 Dec 2021, i.e. ~102 days (~3.4 months); China then took ~60% of Brazil's beef exports.
2023 atypical BSE suspension (Lula govt): beef trade to China halted 22 Feb 2023 and China agreed to resume from 23 Mar 2023 (~1 month), just before Lula's April 2023 China visit.
publisher: Al Jazeera / Bloomberg via Beef Magazine

claim: Australia–China coercion: from May–Nov 2020 China hit Australian barley, wine (tariffs), beef, timber (biosecurity), coal, cotton, lobster (informal bans); impediments were valued at ~A$20bn/yr; barley/coal/timber lifted 2023, wine (28 Mar 2024) and beef 2024, lobster 20 Dec 2024 (~4.5 years).

USSC assesses China's Australia restrictions as 'relatively unsuccessful': cotton, coal and copper were diverted (cotton exports to Vietnam >3x 2018-22), barley went to Middle East at lower prices, wine exports fell 30% (2020-22), and lobster/timber found few alternatives.

Canada canola 2019: China revoked Richardson (Mar 2019) and Viterra licences after the Meng Wanzhou arrest; Canadian canola seed exports to China fell from C$2.8bn (2018, ~40% of the crop's exports) to C$0.8bn (2019), C$1.4bn (2020), C$1.8bn (2021); restrictions lifted after >3 years (2022).

Lithuania 2021: after the Taiwanese Representative Office opened, Chinese imports from Lithuania fell 91.4% y/y in Nov 2021 and Lithuania's exports to China fell ~80% in Jan–Oct 2022; the EU later withdrew its WTO case.

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), 21 Sep 2026 in Natal: relationship with China 'will always be economically pragmatic... we don't have to choose a side', accusing Lula's government of 'declaring war on the US and licking China's boot'; he pledged to negotiate the 55% beef tariff with Beijing.

Foreign Policy reports Flávio's platform pledges to negotiate with China while aligning with the US on security, and endorses barring Pix from 'non-Western cross-border settlement arrangements' (targeting UnionPay integration).

Jair Bolsonaro visited Taiwan in Mar 2018 (Chinese embassy protested) and said as candidate 'the Chinese are not buying in Brazil, they are buying Brazil'; in office he visited Beijing (25 Oct 2019) saying the countries were 'born to walk together'.
Despite rhetoric, Brazilian exports to China reached a record ~US$89.4bn in 2022 (Bolsonaro's last year), vs US$31bn in 2010; China took over a third of Brazil's exports in 2020.

Eduardo Bolsonaro blamed China for COVID (Chernobyl comparison, Mar 2020) and in Nov 2020 tweeted support for a '5G without Chinese espionage'; the Chinese embassy warned of 'negative consequences' to the partnership, but no trade measures followed and Huawei was not excluded from the 2021 5G auction.

Modi made a state visit to Brasília on 8 Jul 2025 (first bilateral PM visit in 57 years) and set a target to raise bilateral trade from US$12.2bn to US$20bn within five years; 6 MoUs signed and both pledged to expand the Mercosur–India PTA.
Lula visited India in Feb 2026: the sides raised the goal to US$30bn bilateral trade by 2030 and signed 10 government agreements incl. critical minerals/steel supply chains, plus 7 private deals.
India and Mercosur launched talks on 14 Sep 2026 to expand their 2009 PTA (currently ~450 tariff lines) and signed a First Additional Protocol on electronic certificates of origin.
Brazil's CNPE approved joining the OPEC+ Charter of Cooperation in Feb 2025 (OPEC welcomed it 18 Feb 2025); the charter is non-binding and does not subject Brazil to production cuts.

Mercosur–UAE CEPA talks were launched Jul 2025; the 4th round ended 7 Nov 2025 with the UAE calling talks 'advanced'; as of early 2026 no agreement had been signed; Mercosur–UAE non-oil trade was US$6.2bn in 2025.

In Dec 2018 the Arab League warned president-elect Bolsonaro that moving Brazil's Israel embassy to Jerusalem would harm Arab–Brazil ties; in Mar-Apr 2019 Bolsonaro retreated to opening a 'business office' in Jerusalem instead.

In Jan 2019 Saudi Arabia (then Brazil's top chicken buyer) delisted 33 Brazilian poultry plants (5 regular exporters incl. BRF, JBS units); 25 plants remained, which had shipped 437 kt (63%) of Brazil's 2018 chicken sales to Saudi; ABPA called it technical, while Arab-chamber figures linked it to the embassy plan.

Brazil exported 5.32 Mt of chicken worth US$9.79bn in 2025 (2024: record 5.294 Mt, US$9.93bn); the Middle East took ~30% (US$3.08bn), with the UAE the top buyer by volume (479.9 kt) and Saudi Arabia third (397.2 kt).

Israel declared Lula persona non grata on 19 Feb 2024 after he compared Gaza to the Holocaust; Brazil recalled its ambassador; Brazilian exports to Israel were US$725m in 2024 (+9.5%, crude 30%, beef 23%) and fell to ~US$569m in 2025 as crude shipments stopped.

Brazil.
